paper_title: A Polynomial Space Lower Bound for Diameter Estimation in Dynamic Streams
authors: Sanjeev Khanna (University of Pennsylvania), Ashwin Padaki (University of Pennsylvania), Krish Singal (University of Pennsylvania), Erik Waingarten (University of Pennsylvania)
source_locator: Explicit open question on PDF page 2
statement: Note that, given prior knowledge of some i ∈ [n] with xi ̸= 0 in the final vector, one could reduce the problem to maintaining distances d(i, j) for updated elements j, and use ℓ0 -sampling [FIS05], [JST11] to estimate the radius around i under insertions and deletions. However, identifying such an i during the stream is challenging: while an ℓ0 -sampler can recover such an index in logarithmic space, its output only becomes available at the end of the stream—too late to maintain relevant distances involving i. Determining the space-complexity of streaming the diameter of a turnstile stream of points in a high-dimensional Euclidean space was asked by Krauthgamer [Kra22]. While this paper does not resolve that problem (which currently remains open), it is a necessary first step.

Complementing this, we give a matching upper bound that achieves a c-approximation in nO(1/c) space for general metrics with polynomially bounded aspect ratio: Theorem 2. For any metric space M = ([n], d) and any c > 6, there is a dynamic streaming algorithm that computes a c-approximation to diamM (x) with Õ(n1/⌊(c−2)/4⌋ ) bits of space.3 The proof of Theorem 2 makes use of low-dimensional ℓ∞ -embeddings and ℓ0 -sampling. Specifically, a result of [Mat96] shows that any metric on n points admits a distortion-(2k + 1) embedding into ℓd∞ with dimension d = O(kn1/(k+1) log n). We show that for dynamic pointsets in ℓd∞ , a constant factor approximation to the diameter be accomplished in Õ(d) space, by maintaining a constant number of ℓ0 -samplers per coordinate.
